scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G# - A - B - C# - D# - E
scalesUsed.application: Primary harmonic foundation for verse and chorus chord progressions
Intro chord-melody arpeggios and clean lead passages
Darker bridge section and emotional climactic passages

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian (Major) with minor color in the bridge

mainProgression.description: Expansive verse progression that moves through the key of E major with a descending emotional arc, creating the reflective mood of the song

sectionProgressions.description: Fingerstyle arpeggiated intro using chromatic voice leading between D, F#, and E major chord shapes high on the neck

sectionProgressions.progression: E - B - C#m - G#m - A - B - E
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - V - vi - iii - IV - V - I
sectionProgressions.description: Full verse progression with gentle strumming building from reflective to hopeful as it resolves back to the tonic
The 'Under the bridge downtown' section centering on the ii chord (F#m) for a bittersweet emotional quality
Chromatic descending progression with modal mixture, shifting from major to minor and back, creating the song's most emotionally intense passage

harmonicFunction: E (I) - Bright major tonic establishing the optimistic foundation
B (V) - Dominant chord providing forward motion and resolution tension
C#m (vi) - Relative minor adding reflective, melancholy color
G#m (iii) - Mediant minor deepening the emotional descent
A (IV) - Warm subdominant providing harmonic contrast and stability
F#m (ii) - Supertonic minor anchoring the chorus with bittersweet quality
Am (iv) - Borrowed minor subdominant in bridge creating dark, chromatic color

techniques.name: Fingerstyle Chord Melody
techniques.description: The intro uses a fingerpicked chord-melody technique where individual notes from chord shapes are plucked to create a flowing melodic line, blending harmony and melody simultaneously

notes: D chord shape at 10th position: arpeggiate individual strings with fingers
F# chord shape at 9th position: hammer-on embellishments between chord tones
E chord shape resolving the phrase
Use thumb for bass notes (strings 6-4) and fingers for treble (strings 3-1)
Each chord shape is voiced high on the neck for a bright, chiming tone
The melody emerges from the top notes of each chord voicing
sequence: Place fingers in D chord shape at 10th fret area
Pluck bass note with thumb, then arpeggiate treble strings with index, middle, ring fingers
Move to F# shape, maintaining smooth voice leading between chord tones
Resolve to E chord shape with deliberate, ringing arpeggios
Allow notes to sustain and overlap for a harp-like effect
tips: Practice each chord shape individually before connecting them
Focus on even finger pressure and consistent volume across strings
Use a clean tone with slight reverb for the authentic sound
Let notes ring into each other rather than cutting them short
Listen to the original recording to internalize the phrasing and timing

techniques.name: Dynamic Strumming with Clean Tone
techniques.description: The verse sections use a controlled strumming approach with clean electric guitar tone, requiring precise dynamic control to move from quiet, intimate verses to full-bodied chorus strumming

notes: E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (standard open E major)
B: X-2-4-4-4-2 (barre chord at 2nd fret)
C#m: X-4-6-6-5-4 (barre chord at 4th fret)
G#m: 4-6-6-4-4-4 (barre chord at 4th fret)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (standard open A major)
Verse strumming is gentle and sparse, building intensity gradually
Chorus requires fuller, more emphatic strumming
sequence: Begin verse with soft downstrokes, barely brushing strings
Gradually increase strumming intensity through the verse
Add upstrokes as energy builds toward pre-chorus
Full strumming with defined pattern for chorus sections
Pull back to intimate fingerpicking for transitions
tips: Control dynamics with strumming hand distance from strings
Use the wrist, not the arm, for gentle verse strumming
Practice the transition from fingerpicking to strumming smoothly
Keep the clean tone crisp - any buzzing is very audible
The song's emotional impact comes from dynamic contrast

techniques.name: Barre Chord Transitions
techniques.description: Smooth transitions between multiple barre chord shapes across different fret positions, essential for the verse and chorus progressions

notes: B barre at 2nd fret (A-shape barre)
C#m barre at 4th fret (Am-shape barre)
G#m barre at 4th fret (Em-shape barre)
F#m barre at 2nd fret (Em-shape barre)
Efficient hand movement between positions is crucial at slow tempo
Each chord must ring clearly - the slow tempo exposes any buzzing
sequence: Practice the B to C#m transition (sliding up two frets)
Work on C#m to G#m (same fret, different shape)
Master G#m to A (barre to open chord)
Build up to performance tempo of 68 BPM
tips: Release finger pressure slightly during transitions, but don't fully lift
Use guide fingers to slide between positions when possible
Practice each two-chord transition in isolation before chaining
The slow tempo makes sloppy transitions very noticeable
Focus on getting clean sound on every string of each barre chord

sections.name: Intro (Chord Melody)
sections.description: John Frusciante's iconic fingerpicked intro, one of the most recognizable guitar intros in rock history, using arpeggiated chord voicings high on the neck
notes: Fingerpicked arpeggios using chord shapes at the 9th-10th fret area
Clean tone with slight reverb - no distortion
Let notes ring and overlap for a harp-like, ethereal quality
This is a solo guitar passage - take your time with the phrasing

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Reflective verse with gentle strumming building from intimate to engaging, supporting Kiedis's introspective vocal melody
notes: Start with very gentle, almost whispered strumming
Build dynamics gradually through each verse repetition
Barre chords must ring cleanly at this slow 68 BPM tempo
Leave space - don't overplay between vocal phrases

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The emotionally powerful the signature section with fuller strumming and the bittersweet F#m-centered progression
notes: Strumming opens up to full, ringing chords
F#m barre chord must be strong and clear as the anchor
Emotional peak of each verse-chorus cycle
Let the final F#m ring with sustain before the transition

sections.name: Bridge / Outro
sections.description: The emotionally climactic bridge and outro section featuring a chromatic descending chord progression with modal mixture, building to the song's most intense moment before the final vocal chants
notes: Chromatic descending bass line creates powerful emotional movement
A to Am shift is the key moment - major to minor color change
Each chord slides down chromatically, building tension
Final E major resolution provides emotional catharsis
Backing vocal chants layer over the repeating progression

guitar.pickup: Single-coil pickups, primarily neck and middle positions for warm, clean tone

effects.distortion: None for intro/verse; light overdrive for bridge intensity
effects.delay: Short slapback delay for intro arpeggios
effects.reverb: Medium hall reverb for ambient, spacious sound
effects.other: Boss CE-1 Chorus (subtle, for the intro chord-melody shimmer). Clean tone is paramount for this song.

beginner.focus: Learn the basic verse chord shapes and simple strumming pattern
steps: Master open E and A chord shapes
Practice basic barre chord shapes for B and F#m
Learn a simplified strumming pattern for the verse
Work on chord transitions at very slow tempo

intermediate.focus: Develop the full verse/chorus with dynamic control and barre chord fluency
steps: Master all barre chord shapes: B, C#m, G#m, F#m
Practice smooth transitions between barre positions
Work on dynamic strumming (soft verse to strong chorus)
Learn the chorus F#m - E - B - F#m progression with proper feel
Add the bridge chromatic descent: A - Am - G6 - Fmaj7 - E

advanced.focus: Master the fingerstyle intro and complete song with authentic dynamics
steps: Learn the fingerpicked chord-melody intro note by note
Develop smooth transitions between fingerpicking and strumming
Add subtle chorus effect for intro authenticity
Practice the complete song with full dynamic arc from beginning to end

commonMistakes: Rushing through the slow 68 BPM tempo - this song needs patience and space
Buzzing barre chords due to insufficient finger pressure
Playing the intro too rigidly - it should feel free and expressive
Not enough dynamic contrast between the quiet verse and full chorus
practiceRoutine: Warm up with barre chord exercises: B, C#m, G#m, F#m transitions (5 minutes)
Practice the intro chord-melody section slowly, note by note (10 minutes)
Work on verse strumming with dynamic control at 68 BPM (5 minutes)
Practice the bridge chromatic descent: A - Am - G6 - Fmaj7 - E (5 minutes)
Play through the full song focusing on the emotional arc and dynamics
focusAreas: Clean barre chord execution at slow tempo
Fingerstyle accuracy and tone for the intro
Dynamic control from whisper-quiet to full strumming
Smooth transitions between fingerpicking and strumming sections
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 68 BPM and practice verse progression with half notes
Practice barre chord transitions with clicks on beats 1 and 3 only
Work on the intro without a metronome first (rubato feel), then gradually add timing
Use metronome for chorus section to lock in the rhythmic drive
